title: add-benchmark-lab-profiling-baselines-and-reporting-pipeline-v85
author: Avery Chen
description: This PR adds v85 of the Benchmark Lab profiling baselines and a lightweight reporting pipeline used by nightly runs. Motivation: recent infra changes (kernel selection and batching heuristics) caused increased variance in cold-start memory peaks for some multi-variant workloads; we need a stable set of baselines and automated reporting to detect regressions early. Changes include: 1) new profiling baseline config files for representative workloads (chat-completion, long-context summarization, embeddings batch) tuned for sequence-length distributions observed in Jan 2026; 2) a reporting pipeline that aggregates perf artifacts from CI and nightly runners, computes summary statistics (p50/p90/p99 latency, peak GPU memory, throughput, KV cache hit rate), and uploads a small artifact + metrics JSON to the profiling-dashboard topic; 3) lightweight adapters to normalize outputs from the new adaptive-batching runner; 4) a set of canonical prompt sets and deterministic eval seeds to reduce noise; 5) CI job updates to run the core profiling suite in a smoke configuration on PRs and full on the nightly pipeline. Testing performed: unit tests for parsers and adapters, integration run against a staging serving cluster for the representative runners (3 full runs to estimate variance), and end-to-end run of the reporting pipeline with synthetic artifacts. Rollout: feature gated behind flag "benchmark_lab_v85" and will be enabled on nightly and canary first; no customer-facing API changes. Linked to ENG-2214 (profiling baselines refresh) and ENG-2231 (reporting pipeline observability).
